ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: On the left side of the figure is a voltage source Vi, with the positive terminal on top and the negative terminal connected to the bottom common node; on the top left there is a 1 ohm resistor, with the voltage V marked across its two ends, the left end being + and the right end being -. The right end of this resistor is the middle top node, denoted as x. The middle top node is connected to the upper end of the right-side 1 A current source through another 1 ohm resistor to the right; the current source arrow points downward, and the bottom end is connected to the bottom common node. The middle top node is also connected to the bottom ground node through an ideal diode, with the diode direction making it conduct when x tries to go below ground and clamp to 0 V. Reasoning: Let the voltage of the middle top node be x, then the voltage at the upper end of the left voltage source is Vi, and the voltage on the required left 1 ohm resistor is V = Vi - x. First assume the diode is cut off, then the 1 A current source will make 1 A flow through the two series 1 ohm resistors on the top, therefore the voltage drop across the left 1 ohm resistor is 1 V, so x = Vi - 1, and V = 1. This cutoff assumption requires the diode not to be forward biased, that is, x >= 0, therefore Vi - 1 >= 0, which is Vi >= 1. Then assume the diode conducts, then it clamps the middle node to ground, x = 0, so V = Vi. At this time the diode current condition corresponds to Vi <= 1. Combining the two regions: when Vi <= 1, V = Vi; when Vi >= 1, V = 1. Therefore V = min(Vi, 1).

raw_record.question_text: In the circuit shown, the diode is ideal. What is the expression for the voltage \(V\) in terms of \(V_i\)?

method.method_draft: Let the middle top node be x. Since the left top node is Vi, the requested resistor voltage is V = Vi - x. First assume the diode is off; then the 1 A current source forces 1 A through the two series 1 ohm resistors, so the drop across the left resistor is 1 V and x = Vi - 1. This off assumption is valid when the diode is not forward-biased, i.e. x >= 0, giving Vi >= 1, so V = 1. Next assume the diode is on; it clamps the middle node to ground, x = 0. Then V = Vi, and the diode current condition is satisfied for Vi <= 1. Combine the two valid regions to obtain V = Vi for Vi <= 1 and V = 1 for Vi >= 1, hence V = min(Vi, 1).
